extracted.intended_audience: readers of Terence Tao's Analysis II (students, instructors, textbook readers)
extracted.subtask_description: A blog page for Terence Tao's Analysis II textbook collecting errata, reader questions/comments, and minor editorial guidance. Contains community-sourced corrections and short instructions for commenting on the blog.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: To enter in LaTeX in comments, use $latex <Your LaTeX code> $ (without the < and > signs, of course; in fact, these signs should be avoided as they can cause formatting errors). Also, backslashes \ need to be doubled as \\.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the inline $latex ...$ wrapper for LaTeX in comments; avoid angle brackets; double backslashes. See the blog 'about' page for further details and the broader commenting policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify edition / page-numbering caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Caution: the page numbering is not consistent across editions. Starting in the third edition, the chapters were renumbered to start from 1, rather than from 12. This has unfortunately caused some ambiguity in the Analysis II text when an Analysis I result was referenced; the above errata attempt to clarify such cases, but the list may be incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referring to page numbers or reporting errata, explicitly state the edition (and ideally chapter/section) because page/chapter numbering differs between editions; when quoting references to Analysis I results in Analysis II, indicate the source edition to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly label references to Analysis I
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple errata entries repeatedly note that references like 'Lemma 8.4.5', 'Proposition 8.4.7', 'Theorem 9.1.24', etc., should be followed by 'of Analysis I' (or similar), to clarify that the cited result is from Volume I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an Analysis II passage cites results from Volume I, append an explicit clarifier (e.g. 'from Analysis I') to the citation to prevent confusion between volumes/edition renumberings. This pattern is repeatedly requested and then added in the errata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errata/reporting precision (page, location, original text, correction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader-submitted errata consistently provide a page number (or chapter/section), the exact original phrasing or display, and a precise suggested correction (often with a short justification). Examples: 'Page 2, Example 1.1.5: “is known the subspace” should be “is known as this subspace”.' or 'Page 28: In Theorem 2.1.4: “Let$f: X rightarrow Y$” is missing a space.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting corrections or suggestions, give the edition (if relevant), the page or precise location (theorem/exercise number/paragraph), quote the original text (or display), state the corrected text, and optionally a brief rationale. This is the format used repeatedly on the page and facilitates quick incorporation of errata ('Erratum added – T.').
